meta.thesis: Concorde was retired because its economics failed three ways at once, not because it was too slow.
meta.misconception_note: The hook states a speed record and beat 2 asks why it stopped, setting up 'it was not one cause'.
meta.visual_anchor: the Concorde supersonic airliner in Air France and British Airways livery at Paris Charles de Gaulle and London Heathrow; only those two airlines' real branding; no other airline, flag or country symbol

host.consent: not a real person: a generated presenter portrait, no likeness of anyone

meta.notes: Illustrative plan. Claims cite Wikipedia (secondary, read 2026-10-20); a real publication needs the primary sources (airline announcements, the BEA report). The crash and the last flight are real events: no AI depiction, licensed archival or code only. The aircraft b-roll is photoreal AI, so the platform AI label is on.

claims.text: The average supersonic transatlantic flight time was just under 3.5 hours.
On 25 July 2000 Air France Flight 4590 crashed, killing all 109 occupants and four people on the ground: 113 deaths.
Air France and British Airways cited rising maintenance costs, low passenger numbers after the crash, and the slump in air travel after the September 11 attacks.
The last commercial Concorde flight was on 24 October 2003.
Speed was not the limiting factor; the cause was economic.
